title: Connect current CRT numerical offsets to the physical Beneš row query
body:
The current CRT RowEntry produced numerical offsets but its caller comparison still used a host logical row query. This package connects that actual offset stream to the unchanged encoded Beneš ROM producer, queries its original physical ROM backing at the current padded coordinate, and returns the micro-row coordinate stream. It disposes of the selected ROM, unused all-layer output, headers and numerical context with explicit local time and retained-backing bounds.

The source-relative proof covers the admitted mixed-width domain, W=P compatibility, successive-right-modulus offsets, current-coordinate countdown, and full successful ownership restoration. Peer review repaired a linear topology-membership scan and a fixed interpreter watchdog. The complete small h=2 pipeline passes normal/optimized and Git-free replay, including the padded-coordinate case, two idle rows, invalid-left identity and four semantic/cleanup fault controls. Exact source and typed-receipt corruption controls reject; committed bytes, source ancestry and36-file export integrity pass.

The separately budgeted four-axis h=4 whole-ROM attempt timed out at180seconds without a completed receipt; ATTEMPT.json records its exact attempted source hashes. No completed h=4 result is claimed. Separate small row invocations use harness input serialization. Full three-epoch key transport, uninterrupted physical whole-level execution, binary numerical lowering and outer multiplication remain open. No selected-frontier or kappa change.

JoyboyBrian, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Retains Ali Romman's RowEntry and all pinned CRT/Beneš/arena predecessor attribution. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4709#discussioncomment-19173182
